newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Bund vols bid up ahead of U.S. data storm.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Bund vols bid up ahead of U.S. data storm.

text.p: Implied volatility of German Bund options on LIFFE nudged higher on Monday as investors prepared for potential upsets ahead of a rush of U.S. data this week, options brokers said.
"With a raft of economic data due later in the week we've seen quite a few people start to buy volatility," said Steven West, options broker at GNI in London.
"The straddle has been bid up," he said.
U.S. data this week include the third quarter employment cost index on Tuesday, third quarter gross domestic product on Wednesday and the widely watched payroll report on Friday.
Brokers quoted implied volatility of December options at around 4.90 percent compared with 4.55 percent for the 100.00 strike on Friday, according to LIFFE.
January, Feburary and March options were all quoted at around 5.0 percent compared with LIFFE's quotes on Friday of 4.69, 4.82, and 4.90 percent respectively.
The December Bund future was quoted at 99.57 at 1224 GMT, down 12 basis points from Friday's settlement. The Bund has been trading in a 99.02 to 99.94 range since the beginning of October.

A broker at a French investment bank said the main trade of the day was by a continental bank which sold 3,000 lots of December 99.00 puts. By 1224 GMT, LIFFE screens showed 4,287 lots had changed hands. December 98.00 puts had attracted volume of 1,200 lots.
Among December calls, the 99.50 strike was the most active, with 968 lots traded.
"Despite the fact we're in a range, despite the fact one bank chucked out all those puts, we're reasonably well bid," the broker at the French bank said.
